title: Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland
author: Lewis Carroll
description: 《爱丽丝梦游仙境》由英国数学家查尔斯·路德维希·道奇森（笔名路易斯·卡罗尔 Lewis Carroll）于 1865 年出版，被誉为世界荒诞文学与儿童文学史上的里程碑。小女孩爱丽丝追赶一只拿着怀表、穿着马甲的白兔，无意中掉进了一个神奇的地下兔子洞。在这个世界里，她通过吃喝奇特的食物变大变小，参加了疯帽客与三月兔的无限茶会，遇到了会隐身的柴郡猫，并与残暴的红心王后展开了一场荒诞离奇的法庭审判。本书充满了语言双关、逻辑悖论与诙谐幽默，是提高英语双关语识别与文学趣味阅读的经典选本。

paragraphs.en: Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank, and of having nothing to do: once or twice she had peeped into the book her sister was reading, but it had no pictures or conversations in it, "and what is the use of a book," thought Alice "without pictures or conversations?"
paragraphs.zh: 爱丽丝在河岸边陪姐姐坐了很久，无所事事，渐渐感到非常厌倦：她偶一两次瞅了瞅姐姐正在读的那本书，但里面既没有插图也没有对话，“要是书里既没有插图也没有对话，”爱丽丝想，“那这本书还有什么用呢？”

paragraphs.en: So she was considering in her own mind (as well as she could, for the hot day made her feel very sleepy and stupid), whether the pleasure of making a daisy-chain would be worth the trouble of getting up and picking the daisies, when suddenly a White Rabbit with pink eyes ran close by her.
paragraphs.zh: 于是她正在心里盘算着（尽她所能，因为炎热的天气使她感到又昏昏欲睡又木讷），做一串雏菊项链的乐趣是否值得她站起来去采摘雏菊，突然一只粉红眼睛的白兔子贴着她跑了过去。

paragraphs.en: There was nothing so VERY remarkable in that; nor did Alice think it so VERY much out of the way to hear the Rabbit say to itself, "Oh dear! Oh dear! I shall be late!" but when the Rabbit actually TOOK A WATCH OUT OF ITS WAISTCOAT-POCKET, and looked at it, and then hurried on, Alice started to her feet, for it flashed across her mind that she had never before seen a rabbit with either a waistcoat-pocket, or a watch to take out of it, and burning with curiosity, she ran across the field after it, and fortunately was just in time to see it pop down a large rabbit-hole under the hedge.
paragraphs.zh: 这并没有什么非常了不起的；爱丽丝听见兔子自言自语地说：“天哪！天哪！我要迟到了！”时，也并不觉得特别离奇；但当那只兔子真的从马甲口袋里掏出一块怀表，看了看，然后急茫茫地继续往前跑时，爱丽丝一跃而起，因为她脑海里突然闪过一个念头：她以前从来没有见过哪只兔子穿马甲口袋，更不用说从里面掏出怀表来了。在好奇心的驱使下，她穿过田野追了过去，幸运的是，正好赶上看到它跳进了篱笆下的一个大兔子洞里。

paragraphs.en: In another moment down went Alice after it, never once considering how in the world she was to get out again.
paragraphs.zh: 下一刻，爱丽丝也跟着跳了下去，压根儿没考虑过将来到底该怎么出来。

paragraphs.en: "Curiouser and curiouser!" cried Alice (she was so much surprised, that for the moment she quite forgot how to speak good English); "now I'm opening out like the largest telescope that ever was! Good-bye, feet!"
paragraphs.zh: “越来越奇妙了！”爱丽丝大声叫道（她是如此吃惊，以至于一时竟忘了怎么说标准英语了）；“现在我像有史以来最大的望远镜一样拉长了！再见，脚丫们！”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, my poor little feet, I wonder who will put on your shoes and stockings for you now, dears? I'm sure I shan't be able! I shall be a great deal too far off to trouble myself about you."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我可怜的小脚丫们，我不知道现在谁来帮你们穿鞋穿袜了，亲爱的们？我敢肯定我是无能为力了！我离得太远了，顾不上你们了。”

paragraphs.en: Just then her head struck against the roof of the hall: in fact she was now more than nine feet high, and she at once took up the little golden key and hurried off to the garden door.
paragraphs.zh: 就在这时，她的头撞到了大厅的顶棚：事实上她现在已经九英尺多高了，她立刻拿起来那把小金钥匙，急忙向花园门跑去。

paragraphs.en: Poor Alice! It was as much as she could do, lying down on one side, to look through into the garden with one eye; but to get through was more hopeless than ever: she sat down and began to cry again.
paragraphs.zh: 可怜的爱丽丝！她侧身躺下，最多只能用一只眼睛透过去看看花园；但要穿过去比以往任何时候都更加没有希望了：她坐下来，又开始哭了起来。

paragraphs.en: "You ought to be ashamed of yourself," said Alice, "a great girl like you, to go on crying in this way! Stop this moment, I tell you!" But she went on all the same, shedding gallons of tears, until there was a large pool all round her, about four inches deep and reaching half down the hall.
paragraphs.zh: “你真该为自己感到羞耻，”爱丽丝说，“像你这么大的女孩，居然这样哭个不停！立刻给我停止哭泣！”但她还是一样哭个不停，流下了成加仑的眼泪，直到在她周围形成了一个巨大的水池，大约四英寸深，漫过了大厅的一半。

chapters.title: Chapter 3: A Caucus-Race and a Long Tale
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 3 章：无结果的赛跑与长故事

paragraphs.en: They were indeed a queer-looking party that assembled on the bank—the birds with draggled feathers, the animals with their fur clinging close to them, and all dripping wet, cross, and uncomfortable.
paragraphs.zh: 聚集在河岸上的确实是一群古怪的家伙——羽毛耷拉着的鸟儿，毛紧贴在身上的动物，一个个全都湿漉漉的，脾气暴躁，极不舒服。

paragraphs.en: The first question of course was, how to get dry again: they had a consultation about this, and after a few minutes it seemed quite natural to Alice to find herself talking familiarly with them, as if she had known them all her life.
paragraphs.zh: 第一个问题当然是如何重新变干：他们对此进行了商议，几分钟后，爱丽丝觉得和他们熟悉地交谈起来似乎非常自然，仿佛她一辈子都认识他们一样。

paragraphs.en: "What I was going to say," said the Dodo in a solemn tone, "was, that the best thing to get us dry would be a Caucus-race."
paragraphs.zh: “我想说的是，”渡渡鸟用庄严的语气说，“能让我们变干的最好办法就是进行一次无结果的赛跑（Caucus-race）。”

paragraphs.en: "What IS a Caucus-race?" said Alice; not that she wanted much to know, but the Dodo had paused as if it thought that SOMEBODY ought to speak.
paragraphs.zh: “什么是无结果的赛跑？”爱丽丝说；倒不是她非常想知道，而是渡渡鸟停了下来，似乎认为总该有人说点什么。

paragraphs.en: "Why," said the Dodo, "the best way to explain it is to do it." First it marked out a race-course, in a sort of circle, and then all the party were placed along the course, here and there. There was no "One, two, three, and away," but they began running when they liked, and left off when they liked, so that it was not easy to know when the race was over. However, when they had been running half an hour or so, and were quite dry again, the Dodo suddenly called out "The race is over!" and they all crowded round it, panting, and asking, "But who has won?"
paragraphs.zh: “哎呀，”渡渡鸟说，“解释它的最好办法就是亲身去做。”首先它标出了一条赛道，大致呈圆形，然后把所有的伙伴散落在赛道的各处。没有“预备，跑”的口令，而是他们想什么时候跑就什么时候跑，想什么时候停就什么时候停，所以很难知道比赛什么时候结束。然而，当他们跑了半个小时左右时，渡渡鸟突然喊道“比赛结束！”他们全都喘着粗气围了过来，问：“但是谁赢了？”

chapters.title: Chapter 4: The Rabbit Sends in a Little Bill
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 4 章：兔子派来小比尔

paragraphs.en: It was the White Rabbit, trotting slowly back again, and looking anxiously about as it went, as if it had lost something; and she heard it muttering to itself "The Duchess! The Duchess! Oh my dear paws! Oh my fur and whiskers! She'll get me executed, as sure as ferrets are ferrets! Where CAN I have dropped them, I wonder?"
paragraphs.zh: 那是白兔子，又慢慢地小跑着回来了，边走边焦急地环顾四周，仿佛丢了什么东西；她听见它自言自语地嘟囔着：“公爵夫人！公爵夫人！哦，我可怜的爪子！哦，我的毛和胡须！她会把我处决的，就像雪貂就是雪貂一样确定！我究竟把它们丢到哪里去了呢？”

paragraphs.en: Alice guessed in a moment that it was looking for the fan and the pair of white kid gloves, and she very good-naturedly began hunting about for them, but they were nowhere to be seen—everything seemed to have changed since her swim in the pool.
paragraphs.zh: 爱丽丝立刻猜到它是在找扇子和那双白小羊皮手套，她非常善意地帮着到处寻找，但到处都找不到——自从她在水池里游过泳之后，一切似乎都变了。

paragraphs.en: Very soon the Rabbit noticed Alice, as she went hunting about, and called out to her in an angry tone, "Why, Mary Ann, what ARE you doing out here? Run home this moment, and fetch me a pair of gloves and a fan! Quick, now!"
paragraphs.zh: 很快，兔子在到处寻找时注意到了爱丽丝，用恼怒的语气对她喊道：“哎呀，玛丽·安，你在外面干什么？立刻跑回家去，给我拿一双手套和一把扇子来！快点！”

paragraphs.en: And Alice was so much frightened that she ran off at once in the direction it pointed to, without trying to explain the mistake it had made.
paragraphs.zh: 爱丽丝吓得够呛，二话不说就朝着它指的方向跑了过去，根本没打算向它解释它犯的错误。

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Advice from a Caterpillar
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 5 章：毛毛虫的忠告

paragraphs.en: The Caterpillar and Alice looked at each other for some time in silence: at last the Caterpillar took the hookah out of its mouth, and addressed her in a languid, sleepy voice.
paragraphs.zh: 毛毛虫和爱丽丝静静地互相注视了一会儿：最后，毛毛虫从嘴里拿出了水烟管，用无精打采、昏昏欲睡的声音向她开口说话。

paragraphs.en: "Who are YOU?" said the Caterpillar.
paragraphs.zh: “你是谁？”毛毛虫说。

paragraphs.en: This was not an encouraging opening for a conversation. Alice replied, rather shyly, "I—I hardly know, sir, just at present—at least I know who I WAS when I got up this morning, but I think I must have been changed several times since then."
paragraphs.zh: 这可不是个令人鼓舞的谈话开端。爱丽丝相当害羞地回答说：“我——我现在几乎不知道了，先生——至少我知道今天早上起床时我是谁，但我想从那以后我一定改变了好几次。”

paragraphs.en: "What do you mean by that?" said the Caterpillar sternly. "Explain yourself!"
paragraphs.zh: “你这么说是什么意思？”毛毛虫严厉地说。“解释清楚！”

paragraphs.en: "I can't explain MYSELF, I'm afraid, sir," said Alice, "because I'm not myself, you see."
paragraphs.zh: “恐怕我无法解释我自己，先生，”爱丽丝说，“因为如您所见，我不是我自己了。”

paragraphs.en: "I don't see," said the Caterpillar.
paragraphs.zh: “我不明白，”毛毛虫说。

paragraphs.en: "I'm afraid I can't put it more clearly," Alice replied very politely, "for I can't understand it myself to begin with; and being so many different sizes in a day is very confusing."
paragraphs.zh: “恐怕我无法说得更清楚了，”爱丽丝非常礼貌地回答，“因为首先我自己就搞不懂；而且一天之内变大变小这么多次，实在太令人困惑了。”

paragraphs.en: For a minute or two she stood looking at the house, and wondering what to do next, when suddenly a footman in livery came running out of the wood—she considered him to be a footman because he was in livery: otherwise, judging by his face only, she would have called him a fish.
paragraphs.zh: 一两分钟里，她站在那里看着那栋房子，纳闷下一步该做什么，这时突然一个穿着制服的仆人从树林里跑了出来——她认为他是个仆人，是因为他穿着制服：否则，单凭他的脸，她会称他为一条鱼。

paragraphs.en: He rapped loudly at the door with his knuckles. It was opened by another footman in livery, with a round face, and large eyes like a frog; and both footmen, Alice noticed, had powdered hair that curled all over their heads.
paragraphs.zh: 他用手关节重重地敲门。门由另一个穿着制服的仆人打开了，那人有着一张圆脸，眼睛大得像青蛙；爱丽丝注意到，两个仆人都留着涂了粉的满头卷发。

paragraphs.en: The Fish-Footman began by producing from under his arm a great letter, nearly as large as himself, and this he handed over to the other, saying, in a solemn tone, "For the Duchess. An invitation from the Queen to play croquet."
paragraphs.zh: 鱼仆人首先从胳膊底下掏出一封巨大的信，几乎和他自己一样大，他把信递给另一个仆人，用庄严的语气说：“给公爵夫人。王后邀请去打槌球。”

paragraphs.en: The Frog-Footman repeated, in the same solemn tone, only changing the order of the words a little, "From the Queen. An invitation for the Duchess to play croquet."
paragraphs.zh: 青蛙仆人用同样庄严的语气重复道，只是稍微改动了一下词序：“王后送来。邀请公爵夫人去打槌球。”

paragraphs.en: Then they both bowed low, and their curls got entangled together. Alice laughed so much at this, that she had to run back into the wood for fear of their hearing her.
paragraphs.zh: 然后他们都深深地鞠躬，他们的卷发缠在了一起。爱丽丝对此大笑不止，以至于她不得不跑回树林里，生怕被他们听见。

chapters.title: Chapter 7: A Mad Tea-Party
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 7 章：疯帽客的茶会

paragraphs.en: There was a table set out under a tree in front of the house, and the March Hare and the Hatter were having tea at it: a Dormouse was sitting between them, fast asleep, and the other two were using it as a cushion, resting their elbows on it, and talking over its head.
paragraphs.zh: 房子前面的一棵树下放着一张桌子，三月兔和帽匠正在桌旁喝茶：一只睡鼠坐在他们中间，睡得很熟，另外两个人把它当成靠垫，把胳膊肘搁在上面，在它头顶上交谈着。

paragraphs.en: "Very uncomfortable for the Dormouse," thought Alice; "only, as it's asleep, I suppose it doesn't mind."
paragraphs.zh: “对睡鼠来说太不舒服了，”爱丽丝想，“不过，既然它睡着了，我想它大概不会介意吧。”

paragraphs.en: The table was a large one, but the three were all crowded together at one corner of it: "No room! No room!" they cried out when they saw Alice coming.
paragraphs.zh: 桌子很大，但他们三个人却全都挤在桌子的一角：“没有地方了！没有地方了！”当他们看到爱丽丝走过来时大声喊道。

paragraphs.en: "There's PLENTY of room!" said Alice indignantly, and she sat down in a large arm-chair at one end of the table.
paragraphs.zh: “这里有的是地方！”爱丽丝愤愤不平地说，并在桌子一端的大扶手椅上坐了下来。

paragraphs.en: "Have some wine," the March Hare said in an encouraging tone.
paragraphs.zh: “喝点酒吧，”三月兔用鼓励的语气说。

paragraphs.en: Alice looked all round the table, but there was nothing on it but tea. "I don't see any wine," she remarked.
paragraphs.zh: 爱丽丝环顾桌子四周，但上面除了茶什么也没有。“我没看到有什么酒，”她说道。

paragraphs.en: "There isn't any," said the March Hare.
paragraphs.zh: “本来就没有，”三月兔说。

paragraphs.en: "Then it wasn't very civil of you to offer it," said Alice angrily.
paragraphs.zh: “那么你请我喝就太没礼貌了，”爱丽丝生气地说。

paragraphs.en: "It wasn't very civil of you to sit down without being invited," said the March Hare.
paragraphs.zh: “你没被邀请就坐下来也不怎么礼貌，”三月兔说。

chapters.title: Chapter 8: The Queen’s Croquet-Ground
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 8 章：王后的槌球场

paragraphs.en: A large rose-tree stood near the entrance of the garden: the roses growing on it were white, but there were three gardeners at it, busily painting them red. Alice thought this a very curious thing, and she went nearer to watch them.
paragraphs.zh: 花园入口附近立着一棵大玫瑰树：上面开着的玫瑰是白色的，但有三个园丁在旁边，正忙着把它们涂成红色。爱丽丝觉得这是一件非常奇特的事情，于是走得更近些去看着他们。

paragraphs.en: Just as she came up to them she heard one of them say, "Look out now, Five! Don't go splashing paint over me like that!"
paragraphs.zh: 就在她走上前去时，她听见其中一个说：“小心点，五号！别把漆溅在我身上！”

paragraphs.en: "I couldn't help it," said Five, in a sulky tone; "Seven jogged my elbow."
paragraphs.zh: “我有什么办法，”五号用闷闷不乐的语气说，“七号碰到了我的手肘。”

paragraphs.en: On which Seven looked up and said, "That's right, Five! Always lay the blame on others!"
paragraphs.zh: 七号听到这里抬头说：“一点没错，五号！总是把责任推给别人！”

paragraphs.en: "YOU'D better not talk!" said Five. "I heard the Queen say only yesterday you deserved to be beheaded!"
paragraphs.zh: “你最好少说话！”五号说。“我昨天还听见王后说你该被砍头！”

paragraphs.en: "What for?" said the one who had spoken first.
paragraphs.zh: “为了什么？”第一个说话的人问。

paragraphs.en: "That's none of YOUR business, Two!" said Seven.
paragraphs.zh: “那不关你的事，二号！”七号说。

paragraphs.en: "Yes, it IS his business!" said Five, "and I'll tell him—it was for bringing the cook tulip-roots instead of onions."
paragraphs.zh: “不，这关他的事！”五号说，“我会告诉他的——是因为给厨师带去了郁金香根而不是洋葱。”

paragraphs.en: Alice stepped up to them and asked softly, "Would you tell me, please, why you are painting those roses?"
paragraphs.zh: 爱丽丝走到他们面前，轻声问道：“请你们告诉我，你们为什么要涂这些玫瑰呢？”

chapters.title: Chapter 9: The Mock Turtle’s Story
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 9 章：假海龟的故事

paragraphs.en: "You can't think how glad I am to see you again, you dear old thing!" said the Duchess, as she tucked her arm affectionately into Alice's, and they walked off together.
paragraphs.zh: “你难以想象再次见到你我有多高兴，你这个亲爱的老好人！”公爵夫人说，一边亲热地把胳膊套进爱丽丝的胳膊里，两人一起向前走去。

paragraphs.en: Alice was very glad to find her in such a pleasant temper, and thought to herself that perhaps it was only the pepper that had made her so savage when they met in the kitchen.
paragraphs.zh: 爱丽丝非常高兴发现她的脾气变得这么好，心里暗想，也许当她们在厨房见面时，只是胡椒粉让她变得那么蛮横的。

paragraphs.en: "When I'M a Duchess," she said to herself, (not in a very hopeful tone though), "I won't have any pepper in my kitchen AT ALL. Soup does very well without it."
paragraphs.zh: “当我成为公爵夫人时，”她自言自语道（虽然语气里没抱太大希望），“我的厨房里绝对一点胡椒粉也不会有。汤里没有它也很好喝。”

paragraphs.en: "You're thinking about something, my dear, and that makes you forget to talk. I can't tell you just now what the moral of that is, but I shall remember it in a bit."
paragraphs.zh: “你在想事情呢，亲爱的，所以你忘了说话。我现在无法告诉你自己其中的寓意是什么，但我一会儿就会想起来的。”

paragraphs.en: "Perhaps it hasn't one," Alice ventured to remark.
paragraphs.zh: “也许它根本就没什么寓意，”爱丽丝冒昧地指出。

paragraphs.en: "Tut, tut, child!" said the Duchess. "Everything's got a moral, if only you can find it."
paragraphs.zh: “呸，呸，孩子！”公爵夫人说。“任何事情都有寓意，只要你能找到它。”

paragraphs.en: "They very soon obliged modify," the Mock Turtle went on, "and then they played the Lobster Quadrille."
paragraphs.zh: “它们很快就不得不修改了，”假海龟继续说道，“然后他们跳了龙虾龙重舞。”

paragraphs.en: "What is that?" asked Alice.
paragraphs.zh: “那是什么？”爱丽丝问。

paragraphs.en: "Why," said the Gryphon, "you first form a line along the sea-shore—"
paragraphs.zh: “哎呀，”狮鹫说，“首先你们沿着海岸排成一条线——”

paragraphs.en: "Two lines!" cried the Mock Turtle. "Seals, turtles, salmon, and so on; then, when you've cleared all the jelly-fish out of the way—"
paragraphs.zh: “两条线！”假海龟大声喊道。“海豹、海龟、三文鱼等等；然后，当你们把所有的水母都从路上清理干净之后——”

paragraphs.en: "THAT generally takes some time," interrupted the Gryphon.
paragraphs.zh: “那通常要花不少时间，”狮鹫打断道。

paragraphs.en: "—you advance twice—"
paragraphs.zh: “——你们前进两次——”

paragraphs.en: "Each with a lobster as a partner!" cried the Gryphon.
paragraphs.zh: “每个人都以一只龙虾作为舞伴！”狮鹫大声叫道。

paragraphs.en: "Of course," the Mock Turtle said: "advance twice, set to partners—"
paragraphs.zh: “当然了，”假海龟说：“前进两次，向舞伴致意——”

paragraphs.en: "—change lobsters, and retire in same order," continued the Gryphon.
paragraphs.zh: “——交换龙虾，按同样的顺序退回，”狮鹫接着说。

paragraphs.en: "Then, you know," the Mock Turtle went on, "you throw the—"
paragraphs.zh: “然后，你知道，”假海龟继续说道，“你把——”

paragraphs.en: "The lobsters!" shouted the Gryphon, with a bound into the air.
paragraphs.zh: “把龙虾！”狮鹫大声喊着，一跃跳到了空中。

paragraphs.en: "—as far out to sea as you can—"
paragraphs.zh: “——尽你所能掷向大海深处——”

paragraphs.en: "Swim after them!" screamed the Gryphon.
paragraphs.zh: “跟着它们游去！”狮鹫尖叫道。

paragraphs.en: The King and Queen of Hearts were seated on their throne when they arrived, with a great crowd assembled about them—all sorts of little birds and beasts, as well as the whole pack of cards: the Knave was standing before them, in chains, with a soldier on each side to guard him; and near the King was the White Rabbit, with a trumpet in one hand, and a scroll of parchment in the other.
paragraphs.zh: 当他们到达时，红心国王和王后正坐在他们的宝座上，周围聚集了一大群人——各种各样的小鸟和小兽，以及整副扑克牌：侍从站在他们面前，戴着枷锁，两边各有一名士兵看守着他；国王旁边是白兔子，一手拿着小号，另一手拿着一张羊皮纸卷轴。

paragraphs.en: In the very middle of the court was a table, with a large dish of tarts upon it: they looked so good, that it made Alice quite hungry to look at them.
paragraphs.zh: 在法庭的最中央放着一张桌子，上面有一大盘馅饼：它们看起来非常美味，以至于爱丽丝看着看着都觉得相当饿了。

paragraphs.en: "I wish they'd get the trial done," she thought, "and hand round the refreshments!" But there seemed to be no chance of this, so she began looking at everything about her, to pass away the time.
paragraphs.zh: “我希望他们赶紧把审判做完，”她想，“然后把茶点发下来！”但似乎没有任何希望，所以她开始看着身边的一切来消磨时间。

paragraphs.en: The King was the judge; and as he wore his crown over his wig, he did not look at all comfortable, and it was certainly not becoming.
paragraphs.zh: 国王是法官；由于他把皇冠戴在假发上面，他看起来一点也不舒服，而且也绝对不合适。

paragraphs.en: "First witness!" cried the King. And the White Rabbit blew three blasts on the trumpet, and called out, "First witness!"
paragraphs.zh: “第一位证人！”国王大喊道。白兔子吹了三下小号，大声呼喊：“第一位证人！”

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Alice’s Evidence
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 12 章：爱丽丝的证词

paragraphs.en: "Here!" cried Alice, quite forgetting in the flurry of the moment how large she had grown in the last few minutes, and she jumped up in such a hurry that she tipped over the jury-box with the edge of her skirt, upsetting all the jurymen on to the heads of the crowd below, and there they lay sprawling about, reminding her very much of a globe of goldfish she had accidentally upset the week before.
paragraphs.zh: “到！”爱丽丝大声喊道，在这一刻的慌乱中完全忘了自己在这几分钟里长得有多大，她急急忙忙地站起来，以至于裙摆碰翻了陪审席，把所有的陪审员全都翻倒在下面人群的头上，他们四仰八叉地躺在那里，这让她非常想起了她前一周不小心碰翻的玻璃金鱼缸。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I BEG your pardon!" she exclaimed in a tone of great dismay, and began picking them up again as quickly as she could.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我真抱歉！”她怀着极度惊慌的语气惊呼道，并开始尽可能快地把他们重新捡起来。

paragraphs.en: "The trial cannot proceed," said the King in a very grave voice, "until all the jurymen are back in their proper places—ALL," he repeated with great emphasis, looking hard at Alice as he said so.
paragraphs.zh: “审判无法继续，”国王用非常严肃的声音说，“直到所有的陪审员都回到他们适当的位置上——所有人，”他重复着，给以极大的强调，说话时狠狠地盯着爱丽丝。

paragraphs.en: Alice looked at the jury-box, and saw that, in her haste, she had put the Lizard in head downwards, and the poor little thing was waving its tail about in a melancholy way, being quite unable to move.
paragraphs.zh: 爱丽丝看着陪审席，看到在慌乱中，她把蜥蜴倒过来头朝下放了进去，可怜的小家伙正以一种忧郁的方式摇晃着尾巴，完全无法动弹。

paragraphs.en: "No, 'they're nothing but a pack of cards!" Alice said loudly. At this the whole pack rose up into the air, and came flying down upon her; she gave a little scream, half of fear and half of anger, and tried to beat them off, and found herself lying on the bank, with her head in the lap of her sister, who was gently brushing away some dead leaves that had fluttered down from the trees upon her face.
paragraphs.zh: “不，他们只不过是一副扑克牌罢了！”爱丽丝大声说。听到这话，整副扑克牌一跃升到空中，然后朝着她飞扑下来；她发出一声小小的尖叫，一半是因为害怕，一半是因为愤怒，试图把它们打掉，结果发现自己躺在河岸上，头枕在姐姐的腿上，姐姐正轻轻拂去从树上飘落到她脸上的枯叶。
